response.consequence: In the rewritten rule list, users cannot pause or export Grafana recording rules from the menu. These actions were available before the change.
response.explanation: The ruler-based useAllRulerRuleAbilities gated ModifyExport, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently on isGrafanaManagedAlertRule, which is rulerRuleType.grafana.rule and is true for both alerting and recording Grafana rules. The new useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities gates them on isAlertingRule, which is prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule and is false for Grafana recording rules. The list view no longer fetches ruler rules, so AlertRuleMenu has only the prom-based abilities there. A Grafana-managed recording rule in the list view therefore gets canPause=false and canExport=false, even for a user with full permissions. No authorization bypass was found. The checks only became stricter, and the permission flags (isEditable, exportAllowed) are still applied.

response.consequence: For federated Mimir rule groups, the UI now reports edit, delete and pause as supported. Users with the matching permissions see those actions enabled where they were previously blocked. Any server-side enforcement is the only remaining guard.
response.explanation: The old useAllAlertRuleAbilities computed isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) from the CombinedRule, so federated rules were treated as immutable and Update, Delete, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently reported NotSupported. The change turns the hook into a wrapper around useAllRulerRuleAbilities, where isFederated is hard-coded to false (TODO). The federated check is not done anywhere on this path, and the wrapper has the CombinedRule available to do it.

response.explanation: AlertRuleMenu calls useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities and ORs their results. The new mocks return one [supported, allowed] tuple per requested action, and the neutral defaults are [false, false]. Each permission test therefore controls the menu items it asserts on. The Grafana tests set the Grafana prom hook and the cloud tests set the ruler hook. The cloud tests also still mock the singular useRulerRuleAbility, which is unused but harmless.
